correctness.rationale: The killed k-subset generator differs from ordinary exclusion by the exact internal-jump killing potential c_k(A)=sum_{u<v in A}(q_uv+q_vu). Finite-state Feynman–Kac gives a path-law RN derivative proportional to exp(-int_0^T c_k(X_t)dt). If equality holds from a single set over one T>0, this integral must be pathwise constant; positive densities of prescribed jump-time simplices and connectivity of the k-subset exclusion graph force every adjacent state to have equal c_k. For 2<=k<=n-2, comparing k-subsets differing in u,v gives equal (k-1)-subset sums of (w_ux-w_vx); index-replacement proves every symmetrized pair weight equal, and positivity/connectivity yields complete support. For k=n-1, c_{n-1}(V\{v})=W-d_w(v); equality iff weighted degrees equal. Four-cycle has one-hole equality but not two-particle equality. Read verifier’s exhaustive n=3,4 and bounded larger-n capacity enumeration; finite enumeration corroborates only small cases.
